title: An Earth-observation satellite
stem: A satellite moves in a circular orbit 630 km above Earth’s surface. Earth’s mass is 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg and its radius is 6.37 × 10⁶ m. G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the gravitational field strength at the satellite’s orbit.
parts.notes: Using the height instead of the radius loses the first mark.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that the orbital speed of the satellite is about 7.5 km s⁻¹.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the orbital period of the satellite in minutes.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: An astronaut on a spacecraft in this orbit reports feeling weightless. Explain this, given that the field strength is not zero.
markscheme: the astronaut and the spacecraft are both in free fall / both accelerate towards Earth at g
the gravitational force provides the centripetal force for both
so there is no (or negligible) normal/contact force between astronaut and spacecraft
the sensation of weight comes from the contact force, so they feel weightless
